fine_trace.note: Attacker-controlled PIZ chunk provides hufbytes=54, which includes a 20-byte Huffman header followed by 17 bytes of table data and 17 bytes of bitstream. The hufbytes value is read from the compressed chunk and passed as nCompressed to internal_huf_decompress.

fine_trace.code: rv = fasthuf_initialize (pctxt, fhd, &ptr, nCompressed - hufInfoBlockSize, im, iM, iM);
fine_trace.note: nBits=129 (>128) enables the fast Huffman decoder path. im=0 and iM=21 are within HUF_ENCSIZE. numBytes=nCompressed-20=17 is passed as the table size, so topByte=ptr+17 marks the end of all available Huffman data.
topByte is set to ptr+17, pointing one past the last valid byte of the 17-byte table/bitstream region. Any read at or beyond topByte is an out-of-bounds heap read.

fine_trace.code: for (uint64_t symbol = (uint64_t) minSymbol; symbol <= (uint64_t) maxSymbol; symbol++)
fine_trace.note: First loop iterates symbols 0 through 21 (22 iterations). The 15 zero bytes produce codes 0-19 all equal to 0 (literal zero, continue). Byte 15 (0xC0) produces code 20=48. Byte 16 (0x0F) produces code 21=63 (LONG_ZEROCODE_RUN).

At iteration 21 (symbol=21), currByte=ptr+16=topByte-1, which is less than topByte, so the bounds check passes. The check only verifies the pointer at the start of each symbol iteration, not before each fasthuf_read_bits call.
fasthuf_read_bits(6) reads byte 16 (0x0F), advancing currByte to ptr+17=topByte. The 6-bit code extracted is 63 (LONG_ZEROCODE_RUN), which triggers a second fasthuf_read_bits(8) call.

fasthuf_read_bits(8) is called with currByte already at topByte. The while loop condition (*bufferNumBits=4 < 8) is true, so it dereferences *currByte at topByte, performing a heap-buffer-overflow read of 1 byte past the end of the allocated Huffman data buffer.

The OOB-read value is used to compute the symbol skip for LONG_ZEROCODE_RUN. The corrupted value causes symbol to exceed maxSymbol=21, leading to the 'Run beyond end of table' error return, but the out-of-bounds heap read has already occurred and is detected by AddressSanitizer.
